title: Ethical consumer decisions

draft.title: Ethical consumer decisions
card: An ethical consumer decision weighs the effects of a purchase on other people and the environment, not only price and quality.
Effects on people can include how workers are treated and paid, and whether children were used as labour to make the product.
Effects on the environment can include pollution, waste and the use of resources such as water and energy.
Ethical choices often come with trade-offs. A consumer may pay more, or have fewer products to choose from, to buy something made in a way they think is fair.
draft.remember: An ethical choice asks who and what a purchase affects, as well as what it costs.

a.q: Which choice is an ethical consumer decision?
opts: Buying a shirt because its maker pays workers fairly
Buying a shirt because it is the cheapest in the shop
Buying a shirt because a friend bought the same one
Buying a shirt because it is on sale this week
a.why: The choice is based on how the product's makers are treated, which is an effect on other people. The other choices are based on price, copying a friend or a sale, and do not consider effects on others.
a.clue: Look for the reason that thinks about other people.

b.q: Noor needs a new phone case. She picks a slightly dearer one made from recycled material over a cheaper plastic one. What does her choice show?
opts: She weighed the effect on the environment against cost
She chose the option that gave her the lowest price
She chose it because the dearer one must be better quality
She avoided any trade-off between cost and ethics
b.why: Noor accepted a higher price because of the lower effect on the environment, so she made an ethical decision with a trade-off. Choosing the cheaper case would have put price first, and the card does not say a dearer product is better quality.
b.clue: Notice what she gave up and what she gained.

a.best: Buying a shirt because its maker pays workers fairly

b.best: She weighed the effect on the environment against cost
